name: Stewed Knuckle of Veal
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: half a pound of salt pork or ham
ingredients.originalText: half a pound of salt pork or ham
ingredients.quantityText: half a pound of salt pork or ham

instructions.text: Put the meat into a pot with two quarts of boiling water half a pound of salt pork or ham cut into strips a carrot two onions a bunch of parsley and one of summer savory all cut fine two dozen whole pepper-corns
Stew closely covered for three hours
When done take the meat from the pot and lay in the dish
Strain the gravy thicken with rice-flour boil up once and pour over the meat

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put the meat into a pot with two quarts of boiling water half a pound of salt pork or ham cut into strips a carrot two onions a bunch of parsley and one of summer savory all cut fine two dozen whole pepper-corns
2. Stew closely covered for three hours
3. When done take the meat from the pot and lay in the dish
4. Strain the gravy thicken with rice-flour boil up once and pour over the meat
